key_concepts: [url]How to make Low Poly Armour for Games (Blender)^^https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C-S0o_mg0No[/url]
Create pauldrons, couters, and vambraces for a low poly mannequin

content: Select the top faces around your shoulder and upper arm (Image 1). [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k], [k]P,S[/k] to duplicate and separate those faces (image 2). Add a Solidify Modifier and adjust the thickness (Image 3).

image.caption: Image 1 - Selecting the top faces around the shoulder and upper arm
Image 2 - Duplicating and separating those faces
Image 3 - Adding a Solidify Modifier and adjusting the thickness

content: In Edit Mode, if you want to adjust the vertices of the pieces, you will only see the original geometry (Image 4). If you want to see the full geometry as it would be with the modifier applied, select [k]On Cage[/k] (Image 5).

image.caption: Image 4 - Going into Edit Mode and seeing only the original geometry without the modifier applied
Image 5 - Selecting On Cage to see the full geometry as it would be with the modifier applied

content: Start by moving the moving the outer edge up to where you want the armour to start and giving it a nice rounder profile (Image 6). Repeat this for the lower rows of vertices in the front (Image 7), top (Image 8), and rear (Image 9).

image.caption: Image 6 - Moving the outer edge up to where the armour should start and giving it a rounder profile
Image 7 - Repeating this for the lower rows of vertices in the front
Image 8 - Repeating this for the lower rows of vertices on the top
Image 9 - Repeating this for the lower rows of vertices in the rear

content: Change the Transform Pivot Point to Median and you can [k]S[/k] to scale the piece (Image 10). You can also use the Shrink/Fatten tool ([k]Alt-S[/k] to create some separation from the base mesh (Image 11).

image.caption: Image 10 - Changing the Transform Pivot Point to Median and scaling the piece
Image 11 - Using the Shrink/Fatten tool to create some separation from the base mesh

content: A recurring trope in fantasy armor is overlapping plates, especially on the shoulders (Image 12). We will attempt to reproduce that. Select the outside edge, [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k], [k]P,S[/k] to duplicate and separate it, and start editing it (Image 13). [k]E[/k] to extrude it out somewhat (Image 14).

image.caption: Image 12 - Showing the overlapping plates trope common in fantasy armor, especially on the shoulders
Image 13 - Selecting the outside edge, duplicating and separating it, and starting to edit it
Image 14 - Extruding it out somewhat

content: Turn on X-Ray Mode, and [k]Alt-S[/k], [k]G[/k] to move around the back edge so it stacks under the first piece (Image 15). Still in Edit Mode, duplicate the piece, move it out and shrink it down for a final overlap (Image 16). Make sure to review it from all sides. At this point, organize your collection and give each object a meaningful name (Image 17).

image.caption: Image 15 - Turning on X-Ray Mode and using Shrink/Fatten and moving the back edge so it stacks under the first piece
Image 16 - Duplicating the piece in Edit Mode, moving it out and shrinking it down for a final overlap
Image 17 - Reviewing from all sides, organizing the collection and giving each object a meaningful name

content: Select the forearm geometry, [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k], [k]P,S[/k] to duplicate and separate it, and start editing it (Image 18). Copy the Solidify Modifier from the pauldron (Image 19). We want to make a cuff at the top, so add a Loop Cut near the top (Image 20). Select the vertices at opposite ends and [k]G,X[/k], [k]S[/k] to move them out and flare them (Image 21).

image.caption: Image 18 - Selecting the forearm geometry, duplicating and separating it, and starting to edit it
Image 19 - Copying the Solidify Modifier from the pauldron
Image 20 - Adding a Loop Cut near the top to make a cuff
Image 21 - Selecting the vertices at opposite ends and moving them out and flaring them

content: Add another Loop Cut down the front (Image 22). Edge Slide the vertices to round out the opening (Image 23). Add a Loop Cut towards the bottom and [k]Alt-S[/k] to shrink that edge and then [k]S[/k] to flare out the bottom (Image 24). Edge Slide the vertices to round out the opening (Image 25). Armour should give room for the user's hand to have full rotation. Last thing, repeat the same rounding of the cuffs in the rear (Image 26).

image.caption: Image 22 - Adding another Loop Cut down the front
Image 23 - Edge Sliding the vertices to round out the opening
Image 24 - Adding a Loop Cut towards the bottom, shrinking that edge and flaring out the bottom
Image 25 - Edge Sliding the vertices to round out the opening
Image 26 - Repeating the same rounding of the cuffs in the rear

content: Select the geometry around the elbows, [k]Shift-D,RMB[/k], [k]P,S[/k] to duplicate and separate it, and [k]Ctrl-L > Copy Modifiers[/k] to copy the Solidify Modifier from the other armour pieces (Image 27). Right now the piece is too big, in Edit Mode, select the outer edge loop and [k]G,G[/k] to Edge Slide it down towards the elbow (Image 28). Slide in the vertices in the front, leaving a larger section in the back (Image 29). Select the back faces, duplicate and separate (Image 30). Increase the Solidify Modifier's thickness and then round it out (Image 31).

image.caption: Image 27 - Selecting the geometry around the elbows, duplicating and separating it, and copying the Solidify Modifier from the other armour pieces
Image 28 - Going into Edit Mode, selecting the outer edge loop and Edge Sliding it down towards the elbow
Image 29 - Sliding in the vertices in the front and leaving a larger section in the back
Image 30 - Selecting the back faces, duplicating and separating them
Image 31 - Increasing the Solidify Modifier's thickness and rounding it out
